newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish exports jump 29 percent in May - exporters.
newsitem.headline: Turkish exports jump 29 percent in May - exporters.

text.p: Turkey's exports jumped 29 percent to $2.23 billion in May, from $1.74 billion in the same month a year ago, reflecting increased demand mainly from the European Union (EU), the Turkish Exporters' Assembly (TIM) said on Wednesday.
Total exports in the first five months of this year rose by 14 percent to $10.5 billion from $9.2 billion in the same 1996 period, TIM said in a statement.

"The positive trend seen in exports in May was mainly due to enlivened demand in foreign markets, particularly the EU countries and the expected positive impacts of Turkey's customs union with the EU," TIM chairman Okan Oguz said.

Turkey's leading readywear exports jumped a record 44 percent to $570.7 million last month, over the same month last year. This was followed by iron and steel exports, up two percent to $259.3 million and textile and related raw material exports, up 31 percent to $270 million.
The biggest increase in May was recorded in exports of leather and leather products with a 68 percent jump to $60.3 million from the same month last year.
Compared to May 1996, hazelnut exports rose by 57 percent to $65.9 million, metal exports by 52 percent to $65 million, grain, pulses and oilseed exports 51 percent to $166.2 million in May.

In the first five months of 1997, readywear exports rose 18 percent to $2.8 billion, iron and steel exports stood at $1.3 billion and textile and related raw material exports at $1.2 billion, both up 11 percent from the same 1996 period.
